passage:
On Saturday, Tushar simply switched off the tablet in the middle of the penguin show. Five-year-old Pema threw herself on the rug and screamed until her face went red. "It wasn't finished!" she sobbed.
On Sunday, Tushar tried something new. "Pema, two more minutes, then it's time to feed the fish," he said, sitting beside her. When the episode ended, he held out the little tub of fish food. Pema pouted and folded her arms. Then she took the tub and ran to the tank on the windowsill of their Kolkata flat, counting the orange fish.

qa.q: What did Tushar hold out when the episode ended on Sunday?
qa.a: He held out the little tub of fish food.

qa.q: Why did Pema scream on Saturday?
qa.a: She felt shocked and angry because the show was cut off in the middle, before it was finished.

qa.q: Which approach worked better, and why?
qa.a: The Sunday one, because the warning and the fish feeding gave Pema time to get ready and something nice to move to.

qa.q: What was Saturday like for Tushar?
qa.a: It was probably stressful and upsetting for him to watch her scream until her face went red.

grounding: It shows a young child melting down when a show ends suddenly, and how a warning and a pleasant next activity soften the change.

passage:
"Nitin, the timer says five minutes left on the racing game," Papa said.
"Okay."
The timer beeped. "That's time, champ."
"No! One more race! Papa, one more!"
"I know. It's hard to stop when it's exciting."
"You're mean!" Nitin stamped his foot and kicked the cushion.
"You're cross. That's okay," said Harish, Nitin's father, calmly. "Want to race me on bikes to the park instead?"
Nitin sulked. "Real racing?"
"Real racing. You can have the red helmet."
A long pause. "I'm going to win."
"We'll see."

qa.q: What does Harish offer Nitin instead of the game?
qa.a: He offers to race him on bikes to the park, with the red helmet.

qa.q: How is Nitin feeling when the timer beeps?
qa.a: He is angry and frustrated at having to stop, so he shouts and kicks the cushion.

qa.q: What did Harish handle well?
qa.a: He gave a warning, stayed calm, named the feeling and offered an exciting real-world activity next.

qa.q: How might Harish feel when Nitin calls him mean?
qa.a: Harish might feel a little stung, but he stays calm and does not take it personally, knowing Nitin is cross about stopping.

grounding: It shows a young child sulking when a game ends and a parent softening the switch with a warning and a fun next activity.

passage: In the Seoul apartment, Soo-ah was halfway through her favourite show when Hiroshi, her father, reached over and switched it off. 'Dinner.' Soo-ah, five, threw herself on the floor, screaming and kicking. Hiroshi was shocked. The next evening he tried something different. 'Soo-ah, two more minutes, then it's finished and we feed the goldfish together.' She groaned. When the show ended, he held out the fish-food tub. She sulked for a moment, then ran to the bowl, sprinkling flakes and giggling as the fish darted up.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah and Hiroshi feed together?
qa.a: The goldfish.

qa.q: Why did Soo-ah scream when the show was switched off?
qa.a: She was upset and frustrated because the exciting show ended suddenly with no warning.

qa.q: What made the second evening go better?
qa.a: Hiroshi gave a two-minute warning and a fun next activity, feeding the goldfish.

qa.q: How might Hiroshi have felt during the first evening's screaming?
qa.a: He was shocked and probably frustrated, not expecting such a strong reaction.

grounding: Shows a young child melting down when a show is stopped abruptly, and how a warning and a pleasant next activity soften the transition.

passage: At the kindergarten, Friday afternoon was movie time. Last week, when the film ended mid-song, Uma, five, had howled and refused to go outside, sulking under the table. This Friday, Chandrika Teacher knelt by the children five minutes before the end. 'When this song finishes, the movie ends and we're going to make giant bubbles in the garden.' Uma frowned but nodded. When the screen went dark, Chandrika Teacher held up the bubble wand. Uma pouted for a second, then jumped up. 'Can I blow first?' Out in the garden she chased bubbles, shrieking with laughter.

qa.q: What did Chandrika Teacher plan for after the movie?
qa.a: Making giant bubbles in the garden.

qa.q: How did Uma feel when the film ended suddenly last week?
qa.a: She was upset and angry, howling and sulking under the table.

qa.q: What did Chandrika Teacher do differently this Friday?
qa.a: She gave a warning before the end and told the children about the fun bubble activity coming next.

qa.q: How might the other children see the change?
qa.a: They probably found the end of the movie easier too, looking forward to the bubbles.

grounding: Shows a young child melting down when screen time ends abruptly, and a teacher using a warning and a pleasant next activity to ease the change.

passage:
Monday: Elizabeth took the phone from Kishore mid-level. The six-year-old screamed, 'I was nearly winning!' and hid under his bed for an hour.
Wednesday: Elizabeth explained, 'Games stop when the timer rings. I'll tell you five minutes before.' Kishore scowled.
Friday: The five-minute warning came. The timer rang. Kishore groaned, but Elizabeth said, 'Want to help me make the chapatis? You can roll the dough.' He handed over the phone and ran to the kitchen, flour on his nose within minutes.

qa.q: Where did Kishore hide on Monday?
qa.a: Under his bed.

qa.q: How did Kishore feel when the phone was taken mid-level?
qa.a: He was angry and upset, because he was nearly winning.

qa.q: What helped on Friday?
qa.a: A five-minute warning, the timer and a fun job rolling chapati dough.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth have felt on Friday compared with Monday?
qa.a: She was probably relieved and pleased that the change went smoothly this time.

grounding: Shows a young child melting down when a game is stopped abruptly, and how a warning and a pleasant next activity soften the transition.

passage: The power went out in the middle of Jyoti's cartoon, just as the rabbit was about to find the key. Jyoti screamed, threw the remote and lay flat on the floor. Noor, her aunt, sat beside her in the dark. "That was sudden. You didn't get to see the end." Jyoti sobbed louder. After a while Noor lit a candle and made shadow rabbits on the wall. Jyoti peeped out from her arm. The next evening Noor said, "Five more minutes, then we feed the parrot." When the show ended, Jyoti grumbled, but she went to find the seeds.

qa.q: What did Noor make on the wall by candlelight?
qa.a: Shadow rabbits.

qa.q: Why did Jyoti scream and lie on the floor when the power went out?
qa.a: She felt upset and cheated because the show stopped suddenly, just before the rabbit found the key.

qa.q: What helped the next evening go more smoothly?
qa.a: Noor gave a five-minute warning and a pleasant next job, feeding the parrot, so the ending was not a shock.

qa.q: What is it like for Noor to sit through Jyoti's meltdown in the dark?
qa.a: It is hard and tiring, but Noor stays calm and kind, naming what happened instead of scolding.

grounding: Shows a young child melting down when a show ends abruptly, and a warning plus a pleasant next activity softening the next transition.
